description:
About the Scholarships

Oregon State University, a public land-grant research university in Corvallis, administers a set of graduate scholarships open to international students each admissions cycle. Funding comes from several directions at once: university-wide awards from the Graduate School, college and departmental scholarships, and named programmes such as the International Cultural Service Program (ICSP), which pairs a significant tuition remission with a cultural service commitment. Because the awards are decentralised, the value and selection criteria differ from programme to programme — some cover a share of non-resident tuition, others pay a fixed annual amount, and a few combine both. Prospective students apply for admission first and are then considered for the scholarships attached to their programme, with some awards requiring a short separate application.

What the Funding Covers

Awards differ in structure. Tuition-remission scholarships reduce the non-resident tuition rate international students pay, which at OSU represents a substantial share of total cost. Fixed-value scholarships pay a set dollar amount towards fees or living costs. Departmental research and teaching assistantships — separate from these scholarships but often awarded alongside them — add a monthly stipend and tuition reduction in exchange for research or teaching work. None of these awards, taken alone, is a full-ride package: students should budget for the gap between the award and the total cost of attendance, including mandatory health insurance.

Eligibility Criteria

  • International applicants (non-US citizens/residents) admitted to an OSU graduate programme.
  • Strong academic record; some awards add leadership, community service or financial-need criteria.
  • ICSP-type awards require a cultural-service commitment (presentations about your home country).
  • English proficiency proof (TOEFL/IELTS or equivalent) as required by your graduate programme.
  • Some departmental awards require separate short applications after admission.

How to Apply

Start by applying for graduate admission to your chosen OSU programme, because most scholarship consideration happens after or alongside the admission decision. Check your department’s financial-aid page for named awards with separate application forms, and submit the international scholarship application on the official graduate scholarships page where required. Applications for the main awards are typically assessed in spring for autumn entry, with 1 May as the commonly cited closing date — but individual programmes can close earlier (dates as early as 1 or 7 April have been cited in some cycles), so verify your exact deadline on the official page before planning.

Important Notes

Oregon State is a popular choice for international graduate students in engineering, computer science, agricultural sciences and forestry, and competition for the larger awards is real. Applicants who also apply for departmental assistantships typically fund their studies more completely than those relying on scholarships alone. Treat the 1 May date as the outer boundary, not the target: finishing your file a month earlier materially improves your chances for awards decided on a rolling basis.
